description: One thing an auditor said to fix, who owns it, when it is due, and whether it was ever actually done. The single most consequential row in this app: an open corrective action nobody can produce a closure for is how a finding becomes a penalty on the next visit.

fields.description: What the auditor found, in their words. Paraphrasing a finding is how a corrective action ends up addressing something the auditor did not say.
fields.label: Finding

fields.description: As the audit scheme grades it. Critical and Major usually carry a deadline the certificate depends on; a Critical left open past its due date is a suspended certificate, not a late task.
fields.label: Severity

fields.description: Closed means the corrective action was done AND there is evidence of it. Nothing sets this for you except close_audit_event, which refuses to close an audit while any action is still open.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Open
In Progress
Closed
Not Applicable

fields.description: The person who is going to do it. Not a department — a person. An action assigned to 'the farm' is an action nobody is doing.
fields.label: Assigned To

fields.description: The date the audit scheme requires it closed by. Most schemes give 28 days for a Major and 24 hours to 7 days for a Critical.
fields.label: Due

fields.description: What was actually changed. 'Trained the crew' is not a corrective action; 'added a hand-wash check to the pre-harvest walk and retrained the four crew bosses on 2026-08-03' is.
fields.label: Corrective Action

fields.description: What proves it: a photo, a training sign-in sheet, a revised SOP's docname, a work order. Where the proof is a Compliance Policy, name it — an audit packet resolves the name and pulls the document in.
fields.label: Evidence

name: Audit Corrective Action
